This walkthrough prepares an ObServe 10.0 longline export to ROS LL 4.2.0, with one Excel form per trip.

## Install R packages

Open R in the directory you want to use for the export. Install `pak` from CRAN if needed.

```{r install-pak, eval=FALSE}
# Install the package installer.
install.packages("pak", repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
```

```{r install-export-packages, eval=FALSE}
# Install the exporter from develop.
pak::pkg_install("ultreia-io/ros.form.observe@develop")
```

## Load the packages

```{r load-export-packages, eval=FALSE}
# Load the reference catalogue tools.
library(form.references)
# Load the form table tools.
library(form.tools)
# Load the ROS form models.
library(ros.form.model)
# Load the ROS catalogue configuration package.
library(ros.form.references)
# Load the ObServe exporter.
library(ros.form.observe)
```

## Export inputs

Exports with the same settings reuse `inputs/` and the catalogue snapshots.

| Input                | Location              | What it defines                                                  |
|----------------------|-----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ObServe form model   | `observe-form.yaml`   | Defines the ObServe tables, their fields and relationships.      |
| ROS form model       | `ros-form.yaml`       | Defines the ROS workbook sheets, their fields and relationships. |
| ROS form template    | `ros-form-empty.xlsx` | Blank ROS workbook to fill for each trip.                        |
| ObServe catalogues   | `observe-catalogue/`  | ObServe code lists and registries used by the export.            |
| ROS catalogues       | `ros-catalogue/`      | ROS code lists and registries used by the export.                |
| Reference mapping    | `mapping.yaml`        | How ObServe codes map to ROS codes.                              |
| Export configuration | `export.yaml`         | Which rows and values to produce for each ROS sheet.             |

## Prepare the input files

Prepare the input files in the ROS target directory.

```{r prepare-export-inputs, eval=FALSE}
# Create settings for the ObServe version, gear and ROS target.
export_settings <- ros.form.observe::export_settings(
  observe_version = ros.form.observe::OBSERVE_VERSION_10_0,
  ros_form_version = ros.form.model::ROS_FORM_VERSION_4_2_0,
  gear = ros.form.model::ROS_FORM_LL,
  output_directory = "output"
)
# Prepare or reuse the input files for these settings.
ros.form.observe::prepare_export_inputs(export_settings)
```

## Load the export context

Each snapshot contains the tables needed by its form model and the selected mapping.

Configure the catalogue URLs in `observe-references.yaml` and `ros-references.yaml` under `inputs/`.
Set any environment variables those YAML files reference for the URLs or credentials.
Use an ObServe catalogue version that matches the source database.

```{r prepare-export-catalogues, eval=FALSE}
# Load both form models, the mapping definition and the export configuration.
export_context <- ros.form.observe::load_export_context(export_settings)
# Prepare the catalogue snapshots, lookups and mapping for reuse across trips.
export_context <- ros.form.observe::prepare_export_references(export_context)
```

Reuse `export_context` for each trip in this R session.

## ObServe connection

Choose one connection method to select trips and extract their tables.

### Public API

Save your ObServe API settings in `observe-api.yaml` and set `OBSERVE_API_PASSWORD`.

```yaml
url: https://observe.example.org/api/public
login: REPLACE_WITH_OBSERVE_API_LOGIN
database: observe
password: !env OBSERVE_API_PASSWORD
```

```{r open-api-connection, eval=FALSE}
# Open a public API session using the YAML settings.
open_observe_api <- function() {
  ros.form.observe::observe_public_api_connect_from_yaml("observe-api.yaml")
}
```

### PostgreSQL

Install and load `RPostgres` for this connection.

```{r load-postgresql, eval=FALSE}
# Install the PostgreSQL driver if needed.
if (!requireNamespace("RPostgres", quietly = TRUE)) pak::pkg_install("RPostgres")
# Load the PostgreSQL driver.
library(RPostgres)
```

Save your PostgreSQL settings in `observe-postgresql.yaml` and set `OBSERVE_DB_PASSWORD`.

```yaml
host: db.example.org
port: 5432
dbname: observe
user: REPLACE_WITH_OBSERVE_DB_LOGIN
password: !env OBSERVE_DB_PASSWORD
```

```{r open-postgresql-connection, eval=FALSE}
# Open a PostgreSQL connection using the YAML settings.
open_observe_postgresql <- function() {
  db.tools::db_connect_from_yaml(RPostgres::Postgres(), "observe-postgresql.yaml")
}
```

## Output directory

Both extraction methods share the catalogue snapshots. Each dated run keeps its own trip selection and source tables.

```text
output/
└── observe-10.0/
    └── ll/
        ├── observe-catalogue/
        └── ros-4.2.0/
            ├── inputs/
            │   ├── observe-form.yaml
            │   ├── observe-references.yaml
            │   ├── observe-sql/
            │   ├── ros-form.yaml
            │   ├── ros-references.yaml
            │   ├── ros-form-empty.xlsx
            │   ├── export.yaml
            │   ├── mapping.yaml
            │   └── correspondences/
            ├── ros-catalogue/
            └── 2026-11-24/
                ├── public-api/
                │   ├── 01-trip-selection/selected-trip-ids.csv
                │   └── 02-source-tables/
                │       ├── <topiaId>/
                │       └── <topiaId>.Rds
                └── postgresql/
                    ├── 01-trip-selection/selected-trip-ids.csv
                    └── 02-source-tables/
                        ├── <topiaId>/
                        └── <topiaId>.Rds
```

Use the export run date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) for the dated folder. Each extraction guide sets the trip dates separately.

## Run the walkthrough

1. Select and extract trips through the [public API](02_extracting_trips_public_api.html)
   or [PostgreSQL](02_extracting_trips_postgresql.html).
2. Use the saved catalogues and trip data to fill a ROS form. See the
   [export configuration](../06-source-coverage/export-configuration.html) for the declared rules.
